steps.what: Identify actual food/beverage samples, sensory specification and required preparation conditions
inputs: actual labelled samples and sensory test method
actual flavour specification or sample-selection characteristics

steps.what: Taste or smell foods or beverages to ensure flavours meet specifications or select samples with specific characteristics
inputs: technician-identified samples and sensory criteria
actual sample tastes and odours under the method
outputs: technician's actual sensory findings and sample-selection judgment

steps.what: Enter and check actual sensory findings and selected sample identities in laboratory sample/test records (OPS_SYSTEM)
inputs: technician's actual sensory findings and sample-selection judgment
actual sample, test and specification identifiers
outputs: exact checked sensory-result entries and sample record destinations

steps.what: Save the exact checked sensory results in the intended sample/test records
inputs: exact checked sensory-result entries and sample record destinations
outputs: saved actual sensory findings and sample selection

tasks.design: Configure sample/test-context identifiers in {OPS_SYSTEM}, the laboratory sample/test record system. The technician handles and assesses actual samples, records the real sensory findings and checks the completed entries before saving them.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated sample/test identity entry adds clerical work to recording sensory findings.
tasks.enabler_now: Native sample-context forms can reuse fixed identifiers.
tasks.still_hard: Taste, odour, sample condition and sensory consistency require the person doing the assessment.
tasks.human_edge: Make and explain the actual sensory judgment.

ambition.what: No synthetic sensory result or automatic product release.

build_days.consent_and_access: 0.5-1; laboratory owner validates sample-context fields and access

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: laboratory sample-context entry can reduce repeated identifiers while actual sensory assessment remains human.

assumptions: Unmeasured recorded sensory-test episode. Gross 24 x .10 = 2.4; upkeep .75; net 1.65 hours per 100.
Actual labelled samples and method already exist; technician identifies them in s1 and produces/captures actual findings in s2-s3. No free digital sensory values or inferred flavour attributes.
Only fixed identifiers/navigation change; substantive observations, selection and final checking remain. No new sample inventory or machine tasting system assumed.

Same-system save 1 is fully retained and earns no saving. Final completed-entry check s3 gates exact records/content; edits require recheck. Do not count the same result entry again under general record compilation.
research_questions: Which sensory record identifiers are retyped rather than already supplied by sample context?

already_counted.description: Sample identification, sensory assessment and actual result entry/check

incremental.description: Maintain and spot-check sensory sample-context fields

approvals.approved_version: Exact completed sensory entries and sample/test destinations checked in s3; edits require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 fixed-entry scenario below 1.65% modeled net; sensory work fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Identify the actual governing-agency record requirements, scope, retention rules and existing laboratory record set
inputs: actual current record requirements supplied by the organisation's quality/compliance owner
actual laboratory test records and required document scope
outputs: technician-identified required records and applicable retention/indexing rules

steps.what: Load and index actual testing results and required documents in laboratory record/document control (OPS_SYSTEM)
inputs: technician-identified required records and applicable retention/indexing rules
actual existing test exports/documents with sample, method and run identities
outputs: loaded actual record set with proposed identifiers and indexing

steps.what: Reconcile required record completeness, source identity, corrections, access and retention treatment, resolving actual missing or mismatched records
inputs: loaded actual record set with proposed identifiers and indexing
actual original results/documents and required-record rules
outputs: technician-reconciled record updates and explicit unresolved gaps

steps.what: Check the final complete required testing-result/document updates, audit identity, indexing and intended retained records
inputs: technician-reconciled record updates and explicit unresolved gaps
actual required-record scope and original documents
outputs: exact checked final retained-record updates and destinations

steps.what: Maintain records of testing results or other documents required by governing agencies by committing the exact checked updates to their intended internal records
inputs: exact checked final retained-record updates and destinations

tasks.design: Configure native identifiers, document indexing and retention fields in {OPS_SYSTEM}, the laboratory record/document-control system. The technician works from actual requirements, loads and reconciles actual records and checks the final complete updates before committing them internally.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated test/document indexing adds record-maintenance administration.
tasks.enabler_now: Native record metadata mappings can reuse identifiers already present in actual source records.
tasks.still_hard: Completeness, corrections and governing requirements require accountable quality judgment.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise missing evidence and preserve the actual record history.

ambition.what: No assertion of legal compliance or autonomous record deletion.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-2; quality/records owner validates requirements, mappings and retention access

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native laboratory record indexing can reduce repeated metadata handling, while completeness and retention decisions require actual organisational requirements.

assumptions: Unmeasured required-record maintenance episode. Gross 30 x .20 = 6; upkeep 1.5; net 4.5 hours per 100.

Actual source test producers already create identified results/documents. Technician loads/indexes and reconciles them in s2-s3; missing or unstructured identifiers require manual capture with no assumed gain.
Quality owner supplies actual applicable requirements; no legal rule is invented from model knowledge. No automated deletion, submission or notification is promised.
Same-system commit 1 stays fully retained with no saving. Completed record-set check s4 gates exact updates/destinations; edits require recheck.
This is maintenance of required records, distinct from initially recording a sensory result. If the same upload/index operation appears in general compilation, count it once across tasks.
unknowns: Actual required-record scope and duplicate indexing
research_questions: Which actual metadata are repeatedly copied and which retention/correction decisions require quality-owner review?

already_counted.description: Requirement identification, reconciliation and final record-set verification

incremental.description: Maintain and validate indexing/retention mappings with the quality owner

approvals.approved_version: Exact final required-record updates, history and destinations checked in s4; edits require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 metadata handling scenario below 4.5% modeled net; no legal judgment or save-click saving.

tasks.short: Analyze results and classify food products

steps.what: Load actual product test results and current standard tables in laboratory results/specification software (OPS_SYSTEM), checking sample and method identities
inputs: actual identified instrument/analyst test result exports
actual current approved standard tables from their quality owner
outputs: technician-checked source test rows and applicable standard-table version

steps.what: Compare actual test results with applicable standard tables using their exact units, method, limits and classification rules
inputs: technician-checked source test rows and applicable standard-table version
actual approved comparison formulas and exception rules
outputs: computed candidate comparisons and explicitly flagged missing/ambiguous cases

steps.what: Analyze test results to classify products, resolve actual exceptions and enter/check final classification, supporting evidence and intended product record
inputs: computed candidate comparisons and explicitly flagged missing/ambiguous cases
actual original results, applicable standards and delegated classification authority
outputs: exact checked final product classification with evidence and intended record

steps.what: Save the exact checked product test classification in the intended internal product/test record
inputs: exact checked final product classification with evidence and intended record

tasks.design: Configure native result imports and exact approved table comparisons in {OPS_SYSTEM}, the laboratory results/specification system. The technician checks source and standard identity, reviews comparisons, resolves exceptions and checks the final classification before saving it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated result entry and table lookup/calculation add analysis handling.
tasks.enabler_now: Native specification rules can calculate explicit comparisons over stable structured records.
tasks.still_hard: Wrong method, units or applicable standard can produce a precise but invalid classification.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise inappropriate comparisons and unresolved product cases.

ambition.what: No autonomous product release or classification outside delegated authority.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-2; quality owner validates standard versions, rules and classification authority

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native laboratory specification rules can compare structured results with fixed approved tables, with applicability and exceptions reviewed by the technician.

assumptions: Unmeasured currently manual comparison episode. Gross 25 x .20 + 35 x .30 = 15.5; upkeep 3; net 12.5 hours per 100.

Instrument/analyst produces actual identified test exports; quality owner maintains actual standard tables. Technician loads/checks sources in s1 and resolves/records conclusions in s3. Missing schema, method or limits stop automated comparison for manual handling.
No LLM arithmetic or inferred limit. Existing configured comparisons already used today earn no new saving; proposed gain applies only to currently repeated entry/lookups.

Same-system save 1 is fully retained and earns no saving. Completed exact classification/evidence/destination check s3 gates s4; edits invalidate it. No product shipment, release notification or laboratory retest action is promised.
Do not add the same result-import saving again under record compilation or required-record maintenance.
unknowns: Actual comparison rules already configured and manual exception rate
research_questions: Can exact native rules reproduce current classifications while explicitly refusing method/unit/version mismatches?

already_counted.description: Remaining source/comparison checks, exception resolution and final classification entry/check

incremental.description: Maintain and regression-check result mappings and standard-table versions/rules

approvals.approved_version: Exact completed classification, supporting comparison evidence and destination checked in s3; edits require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 explicit table-comparison scenario below 12.5% modeled net; final classification and exceptions remain human.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compile food test graphs and reports

steps.what: Load and reconcile actual identified food/beverage test results for the requested graph or report scope in laboratory reporting software (OPS_SYSTEM)
inputs: actual existing structured instrument/analyst result exports
actual requested sample, method, run and reporting scope
outputs: technician-checked actual result dataset with source identities

steps.what: Record or compile test results and prepare graphs and charts with actual units, sample grouping, axes and requested summary tables
inputs: technician-checked actual result dataset with source identities
technician-selected actual graph grouping, axes and summary requirements
outputs: candidate actual result tables, graphs and charts

steps.what: Prepare and check the complete test report, actual result annotations, units, omissions, chart interpretation and intended internal report record
inputs: candidate actual result tables, graphs and charts
actual original results and requested scope
outputs: exact complete checked test report with actual charts and destination

steps.what: Save the exact checked compiled test report and charts in the intended internal report record
inputs: exact complete checked test report with actual charts and destination
outputs: saved internal food-test report and charts

tasks.design: Configure native result imports, graph profiles and table templates in {OPS_SYSTEM}, the laboratory reporting system, and {SPREADSHEET}. The technician selects actual scope and chart choices, reconciles source data and writes/checks the complete report in {DOCS} before saving it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated rebuilding of result tables and charts adds reporting effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Native report/graph profiles can reuse a stable result schema and recurring display structure.
tasks.still_hard: Chart grouping, omissions and interpretation can misrepresent real test outcomes.
tasks.human_edge: Choose a faithful display and explain actual limitations.

ambition.what: No autonomous result interpretation or external report release.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-2; laboratory reporting owner validates exports and graph profiles

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native laboratory graph/report profiles can reduce repeated structured result assembly, while data validity and interpretation require technician review.

assumptions: Unmeasured recurring report episode that currently rebuilds tables/plots. Gross 25 x .20 + 45 x .40 = 23; upkeep 3; net 20 hours per 100.

Actual test producers already create identified exports; technician captures/reconciles the reporting dataset in s1 and makes grouping/axes choices in s2. Missing or changed schema requires manual work; no free structured results assumed.

Native graph calculation already used today earns no saving; only repeated setup/assembly changes. Narrative annotations and full-report checking remain in s3; no LLM arithmetic or generated scientific claims.
Same-system save 1 remains fully retained with no saving. Final complete report/chart check s3 gates exact internal version/destination; edits require recheck. No external send is promised.
Use this once for the actual compiled report. Shared imports and result entry with analysis, sensory recording or required-record maintenance must be deduplicated in a role roll-up.
unknowns: Actual repeated chart setup and overlap with other record tasks
research_questions: Which charts are rebuilt rather than refreshed from existing profiles, and which import operation is shared?

already_counted.description: Remaining dataset/graph checking, actual annotations and complete report verification

incremental.description: Maintain and test result schema, graph profiles and report templates

approvals.approved_version: Exact completed report, tables, graphs and destination checked in s3; edits require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 repeated report-assembly scenario below 20% modeled net; zero when charts/imports are already configured.
